segments.text: Logic, level three. We come in as level3 - the Caesar shift from level two worked - and the first question, as always, is what the challenge binary looks like. Except this time the answer is already known to be grim: the level directories on this box have been player-managed for years, and level three's is empty.

Listing slash levels slash level3: total eight, no entries beyond dot and dotdot. The directory itself is d r minus x minus - - - r w x - world-writable other perms, untouched since August twenty-twenty-two. A challenge directory that anyone can write and that contains nothing is not a puzzle; it is a crime scene.

The home directory tells the rest: dot pass, dot bash history at thirty-two kilobytes, a dot viminfo full of gdb and exploit-typing history, and a seven-byte file called tags, group-owned by level2, containing exactly one word: Letsgo.

And in the bash history - nine hundred plus lines of prior players' gdb sessions, nopsleds and return addresses aimed at a level3 binary that no longer exists - sits the confession, in the player's own words: quote, accidentally deleted the executable, was a bit frustrated and was curious whether the permissions were so broken that I could delete the level exec. Im sry :( end quote - echoed into a sorry dot txt that is itself long gone.

Due diligence, anyway: a full-filesystem find for anything group level3 returns only the empty slash levels slash level3 directory itself; anything owned by level4 returns only the closed slash levels slash level4 directory. Nothing to pivot through.

The setuid sweep confirms it: every suid binary on the box is a stock operating-system one - mount, su, ping, umount, unix_chkpwd, crontab, passwd, sudo and friends. No level binary, no backdoor, no path from level3 to level4 survives on this machine.
Even the previous level's source, readable a minute ago as level2, is now closed to us - permission denied - so the box has literally nothing left to teach at this level.

So level three is documented-blocked, exactly like blowfish level three was: destroyed server-side by a player years ago, with the confession preserved in the shell history. We confirm our standing on the level with cat tilde slash dot pass - P I Z I P M W K E C, the password we already earned - and record this cast as the evidence entry. The numbering stays contiguous; the solve, when the staff ever restore the binary, will be the classic strcpy overflow the deleted binary was famous for.
